9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: Medium close-up from a slightly elevated angle, 85mm macro lens, 16:9 composition. Scarlett (Image 2) stands at the black stone sink, holding the closed coral lipstick upright in both hands beside her mouth, thumb poised beneath the casing just before the decisive twist, weight settled toward the vanity and eyes fixed on the mirror. Her lips and hands dominate the foreground, while the mirror catches a partial reflection and leaves open space toward the sink for the next application. Compact contemporary bathroom with white tiled walls and restrained counter details. Hard morning sunlight cuts diagonally across tile and sink, catching the metal casing with a crisp highlight. Clean, bright, tactile editorial product photography, natural color, shallow focus, airy shadows.

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
Image 3 (location): INT. DOWNTOWN APARTMENT BATHROOM — MORNING - Compact contemporary apartment bathroom with white tiled walls and a black stone sink
